mark_affecting.quote: The ship actually manages to destroy one of the tripods... It's one fleeting victory that ultimately changes nothing.
You have the haunting, unearthly 'ulla, ulla' cry of the tripods echoing around.

flagged.title: Book 2: Survival & Resolution
flagged.reason: The video prominently presents fabricated quotations on screen and in narration for both the curate ('What has God wrought?') and the novel's final reflection ('We can never regard this earth as the entire universe...'), which would penalise students in a GCSE English Literature exam.

mark_affecting.quote: Why are these permitted? ... What has God wrought?
We can never regard this earth as the entire universe... as we did before.

flagged.title: Science Fiction Genre & Structure
flagged.reason: The video explicitly tells students to memorize the fabricated quote 'I did not know then what I know now', which does not appear in the novel and would penalize a GCSE student citing it.

mark_affecting.quote: And here is a highly citable top-tier quote I really want you to memorize right now: 'I did not know then what I know now'

flagged.reason: The video extensively teaches AO4 as an assessed objective on this question (costing marks for SPaG and securing AO4 marks), directly contradicting the corrected specification where this paper assesses only AO1, AO2, and AO3.

mark_affecting.quote: And lastly, we have AO4: accuracy of written expression. Depending on your specific exam board's mark allocation, careless spelling, punctuation, and grammar will literally cost you marks.
